title: Visiting at night
translation: Temples and shrines too: go on a day when nobody else goes, and go at night.
original: {神仏|かみほとけ}にも、{人|ひと}の{詣|まう}でぬ{日|ひ}、{夜|よる}まゐりたる、よし。
literal: To the gods and buddhas too, going on a day when people do not visit, at night, is good.

notes.text: {神仏|かみほとけ}: 'gods and buddhas', so shrines and temples. In Kenkō's time the two were closely mixed, and many shrines had temples attached. も 'too' links this one sentence to section 191: like people, holy places are better at night.
{詣|まう}づ: to visit a shrine or temple. On festival days and the days sacred to a particular god or buddha, the crowds came. Kenkō prefers the other days.
The whole section is one sentence, and the verdict is a single plain word: よし, 'good'.
